Testimony of the Maine Municipal Association (MMA)
In Support of LD 1235, An Act to Establish Transparency in Opioid Settlement Funds
Allocated to Municipalities or Counties
April 3, 2025 ________________________________________________________________
Senator Ingwersen, Representative Meyer and distinguished members of the Joint Standing Committee on Health and Human Services, my name is Amanda Campbell, and I am submitting testimony in support of LD 1235 on behalf of the Maine Municipal Association's 70-member Legislative Policy Committee (LPC).
LD 1235 directs municipal, and county governments identified as direct share plaintiff subdivisions receiving opioid settlement funds to file required annual reports outlining the expenditures of those settlement funds.
Municipal officials managing these settlement funds have been provided with extensive guidance from the Office of the Maine Attorney General*, including resources from MMA's partner, the National League of Cities, as well as the Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health and the National Association of County and City Health Officials. The approved usages of settlement funds are outlined in the Maine Subdivision 2022 and 2023 Memorandum of Understanding Regarding Opioid Settlement Funds*.
Reporting the expenditure of these funds, in accordance with the legal documents governing the settlement, is a task that municipal officials support.
Thank you for your consideration of the municipal perspective on this important topic. Please feel free to contact any member of the LPC or the MMA Advocacy team with any questions relating to municipal operations.
*https://www.maine.gov/ag/opioids/resources.html *https://www.maine.gov/ag/opioids/index.html

Good afternoon, Senator Ingwersen, Representative Meyer and distinguished members of the
Health and Human Services Committee. My name is Amy Roeder, and I represent House District
23, which includes a portion of the great City of Bangor.
I am here today to introduce LD 1235, An Act to Establish Transparency in Opioid
Settlement Funds Allocated to Municipalities or Counties.
This is a simple bill that would require an annual report to be submitted to the Attomey General
that details how opioid settlement funds are received and expended by municipalities or counties,
with a detailed description of each expenditure.
This entire committee is aware of how crucial these funds are in helping commmiity members who are recovering from substance use disorder. To ensure that this population is being served to the best of our ability here in Maine, we must track how this money is used.
I understand that this committee completed the public hearing and work session process for a
similar bill, LD ll0, An Act to Require Reporting on the Expenditure of Opioid
Settlement Funds by Certain Municipalities and County Governments.
This measure, however, is a bit different. I would like to offer a friendly amendment that would direct all accrued interest to be returned to the Attorney General's opioid settlement funds.
In Bangor, we have seen the city pocket the interest from these funds. As of now, Bangor has no plans on how to distribute opioid settlement funds, nor do they have a special committee or council set up to advise the city. Moreover, when asked about using settlement funds to keep the

District 23: Part of Bangor

Hope House open, Bangor legislators were told that Bangor already spent all of its opioid settlement funds on a $30K syringe cleanup program.
It is crucial that there be transparency in how these funds are spent. This is helpful for all parties and ensures that those held accountable for spending the funds do so in a way that is responsible
and will ultimately be helpful for community members recovering from substance use disorder.
Thank you for your consideration. I am happy to answer any questions you may have.

Addendum to the Maine Municipal Association's Testimony
Amended Version of
LD 1235, An Act to Establish Transparency in Opioid Settlement Funds Allocated to Municipalities or
Counites
April 3, 2025
Senator Ingwersen, Representative Meyer and members of the Health and Human Service -Committee, my
name is Kate Dufour, and I am submitting an addendum to MMA s previously submitted testimony on
LD 1235 for two reasons.
The first is that the amendment being advanced by the bill's sponsor is a significant departure from the
originally printed bill and one that MMA's Legislative Policy Committee has not had an opportunity to
review. As indicated in the association's position on LD 110, municipal officials understand the need for
transparency and the reporting requirements associated with the use of opioid settlement funds. However,
we are not sure how our members would react to the investment and remittance requirements proposed in
the amended version of LD 1235.
Second, from a staff perspective, we question the efficacy and reason for requiring municipalities to place
funds in interest bearing accounts, only to have the state reap the resulting benefits. If the state feels that these funds should be invested in ways that generate additional income, then at the very least those resulting revenues should be used to support the programs developed locally via use of the settlement
funds.
Additionally, there is nothing that would prevent the state from investing and using its revenue as proposed in the amendment.
Thank you for your consideration of the concerns raised in MMA's testimony. Should our policy
committee have an opportunity to review the amendment for LD 1235 prior to the bill's work session, we
will submit additional testimony for your consideration.

Dear Senator Henry Ingwersen, Representative Michele Meyer, and distinguished members of the Joint Standing Committee on Health and Human Services,
My name is Michael Beck, and I am a resident of Bangor. I support LD 1235, "An Act to Establish Transparency in Opioid Settlement Funds Allocated to Municipalities or Counties." I respectfully request that you vote 'ought to pass' on this bill.
Transparency is non-negotiable; the public has an absolute right to know how opioid settlement funds--funds derived from immense suffering--are being utilized. I have heard some counties/municipalities are claiming that this reporting constitutes an undue burden. I, as an individual, maintain a list of the city of Bangor's Opioid Settlement Funds expenditures on my personal website.
https://bangormike.com/opioid-settlement-payments-received-expenditures-by-bangor-maine/
Shortlink: https://bangor.link/BangorOSF
If I can achieve this level of transparency as a citizen, certainly municipalities and counties can. And they should. This bill is essential for accountability to those who have suffered the most in this opioid crisis. Please pass it.
Sincerely,
Michael Beck Bangor

10042017:
Testimony in Support of LD 1235: An Act to Establish Transparency in Opioid Settlement Funds Allocated to Municipalities or Counties
April 3, 2025
Senator Ingwersen, Representative Meyer, and Honorable Members of the Committee on HHS,
My name is Tess Parks. I am the Policy Director of the Maine Recovery Action Project (ME-RAP), a grassroots network of Mainers working on community and public policy based solutions to substance use. I am here today to testify in support of portions of LD 1235 on behalf of our statewide team of organizers.
Our organizing team has not yet had the opportunity to review the sponsor's amendment language so I am not prepared to share our position on that portion of the proposal. However, our team remains in strong support of the policy goal to ensure all recipients of opioid settlement funds (OSF) publicly report what they receive and how they spend it. We deeply appreciate the leadership of Rep. Roeder and Rep. Brennan in advancing legislation that strengthens OSF transparency at both the municipal and county levels, as well as each of you for the unanimous vote on LD 110 last week.
Over the last week, our network of partners working on OSF transparency alerted us to pending legislation in Maryland, HB07981, which is currently awaiting the Governor's signature. This bill includes specific public reporting requirements, including the creation of a public dashboard that must display: (1) a payment schedule of estimated OSF disbursements to the state, counties, and municipalities; (2) past spending of OSF; (3) spending plans and funding priorities; and (4) detailed descriptions of initiatives funded by the settlement, including performance metrics where applicable.
While Maine's Opioid Settlement MOU2 requires the Maine Recovery Council to "develop a centralized public dashboard . . . for public expenditure data from any part or regional council that received recovery funds," it does not clearly define the types of data that must be collected and reported. We request that you consider adding more specific reporting requirements to the OSF reporting required in this legislation. This will ensure that advocates, lawmakers, and the public have a clear understanding of what is happening across the State relating to OSF spending.
Having a clear set of reporting guidelines will enhance transparency, accountability, and public trust in how these critical funds are used.
Thank you for your time and consideration.
